subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should `.bak.*` session archives be automatically pruned or retained as recovery/debug artifacts, and under what retention boundary?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves old `.bak.*` archives in maintenance coverage, while this issue asks for automatic cleanup across all stale session artifact classes.

options.title: Prune bounded `.bak.*` archives
options.body: Add explicit `.bak.*` retention or per-base rotation in session maintenance with tests proving active transcripts and recovery-needed backups survive.

options.title: Keep `.bak.*` as recovery artifacts
options.body: Document that `.bak.*` files are manually managed recovery artifacts and narrow this issue to deleted/reset/temp cleanup only.

recommendation.title: Prune bounded `.bak.*` archives
recommendation.body: Add explicit `.bak.*` retention or per-base rotation in session maintenance with tests proving active transcripts and recovery-needed backups survive.

likelyOwner.reason: The local history shows the strongest prior ownership of session maintenance policy and cleanup UX.
